boundaries.decoded_bitmap: Parent validator addresses, LastCommit flags and live-seat words are decoded inputs. Header and storage authentication, stock CometBFT integration and execution refinement are external.
boundaries.weighted_quorum: Both quorums use one supplied list of members and their voting powers. Commit validation, signer attribution, committee authentication and stake backing are external.

claims.description: A successful decoded non-initial bitmap sets a bit exactly when a parent validator with a non-COMMIT flag maps to that live seat. Every bit at seat 128 or higher is clear.
Two strict two-thirds quorums over one supplied weighted member list share more than one third of its total voting power.

BACKP-6.4-1.reason: A decoded height accepted by the bound check has at most U blocks above the supplied checkpoint. Anchor and checkpoint authentication remain external.

BACKP-6.4-2.reason: The target constant satisfies the decoded range for U. Encoding and config-hash binding remain external.

BACKP-6.4-4.reason: The modeled target U = 151200 passes the range check. Deployment selection and time estimates remain external.

COMM-4.3-1.reason: Both initial heights use the origin commitment. Each later signing set comes from the decoded decision input two heights before.

COMM-4.3-13.reason: An accepted decoded validator advance increments the height and promotes the prior next set unchanged. Stock CometBFT integration remains external.

COMM-4.3-18.reason: An accepted decoded threshold update requires the configured owner as caller.

COMM-4.3-3.reason: Successful decoded staking transactions preserve the already-written candidate snapshot and generation.

COMM-4.3-3a.reason: An accepted candidate matches the full height word, meets the stake threshold and has a valid snapshot. The sentinel selects fallback independently of snapshot fields.

COMM-4.3-8.reason: Accepted decoded members satisfy the valid-set predicate and come from exactly 128 snapshot records.

COMM-4.3-8b.reason: An accepted decoded fallback opening authenticates the ordered keys against the supplied hash and assigns every key unit power.

COMM-4.3-9.reason: The signing accessor and the decoded guest boundary both derive the first two sets from the fixed origin fallback commitment.

CONS-3.2-13.reason: A rejected block-start transition leaves its input state intact. EL call ordering, gas, and block rejection remain external.

CONS-3.4-7a.reason: Decoded first-block flags are empty and the bitmap is zero. Later bits mark precisely the mapped misses, with every bit at or above seat 128 clear.

FORF-4.4-13.reason: A successful decoded transaction, including forfeiture, preserves the already-written staking snapshot.

FORF-4.4-7.reason: Decoded forfeiture arithmetic rounds the product up and stays within principal for a rate at most 10000 basis points.

PROOF-6.2-12a.reason: The decoded boundary derives p + 1 from the fixed fallback opening at the origin and the next height. After that it checks the supplied members against the opened header’s next validator hash.

PROOF-6.2-12b.reason: The decoded boundary derives p + 2 from the fixed fallback opening at the origin, or from the committee decision given the parent input opened at the checkpoint EL hash.

PROOF-6.2-12c.reason: The decoded boundary has no parent set at the origin. At a later checkpoint it checks the supplied parent members against the validator hash of the opened header.

PROOF-6.2-16.reason: The decoded gate compares key-power membership independently of order and requires a qualifying commit at the terminal height or a set change. Proof execution remains external.

PROOF-6.2-17.reason: A required decoded commit needs distinct members backed by matching precommits and more than two-thirds of the supplied power. Two strict quorums on the same set share more than one third of that power. Signature verification and committee authentication are supplied interfaces.

PROOF-6.2-47.reason: The decoded boundary opens the parent decision at the checkpoint height and EL hash and reads its snapshot and anchor inputs for p + 2. L1 witness validation and inherited-anchor checks remain external.

RECOV-8.4-13.reason: The decoded anchor guard requires the anchor block number to be at or above the fixed origin. L1 finality and root authentication remain external.

RECOV-8.4-3.reason: A successful decoded origin write records the Inbox fallback hash at that write.

RECOV-8.4-4.reason: A successful decoded origin write preserves the lookup for every other generation.

STAKE-4.1-28a.reason: The accepted delay is at least U + 2 + the evidence window. Checkpoint progress and transaction inclusion remain external.

STAKE-4.2-6.reason: Decoded miss-penalty arithmetic rounds the product up and stays within principal for a rate at most 10000 basis points.

STAKE-4.2-7.reason: A successful block start writes the current height and 128 records. Successful decoded transactions leave that snapshot unchanged.
